title: Share a page's link from Chrome onto a contact

setup.why: No contact with this run's nonce is left from an earlier try.
The contact the link goes onto: a name and a phone number, no website.
Grant the contacts apps their permissions, so the agent doesn't meet a permission prompt the task isn't about.

argv: for p in com.google.android.contacts com.android.contacts com.samsung.android.app.contacts; do pm grant $p android.permission.READ_CONTACTS 2>/dev/null; pm grant $p android.permission.WRITE_CONTACTS 2>/dev/null; done; true

setup.why: Stop a server an earlier try left on this port (the bracket keeps pkill's pattern from matching this shell).
Write the HTTP answer: the contact's page, with this run's nonce on it.
Serve the page on the phone's loopback, and prove it is served before the agent starts.
Open the page in Chrome, in the bench's tab: the agent starts on it.

instruction: Chrome is showing {{who.first}} {{who.last}}'s page. Use Chrome's Share menu to copy the page's link, then open the contact "{{who.first}} {{who.last}} {{nonce}}" in Contacts, paste the link into its website field, and save.

checks.why: Prints the contact's website rows, then its phone rows. A website holds the page's address (127.0.0.1:{{port}}, with or without http:// and a closing slash), and the phone setup gave it (303 555 0142) is still there, so the link went onto this contact rather than a new one. Setup gave it no website, so an agent that does nothing fails.
argv: sh -c "$1" sh websites "$2"; sh -c "$1" sh phones "$2"

teardown.why: Delete every contact holding the nonce, stop the run's server and delete its files.

argv: sh -c "$1" sh purge {{nonce}}; pkill -f 'nc -L -p {{port}}[ ]'; rm -f /data/local/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}.http /data/local/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}.sh; true
